From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo today — quick follow-ups

Jordan — great to hear, and thanks for the clear priorities. I chatted with Rafael and Neha and put together the shortlist + rationale below. Attaching the prompt set + evals so your team can reproduce.

Quick summary (shortlist + one-line rationale):
1) Redwood-Instruct-13B-v1 — Best quality/cost balance for knowledge-grounded answers; tuned for instruction-following; fallback if you need higher accuracy.
2) Llama-2-13B-chat (quant q4f16) — Strong semantic accuracy, slightly lower throughput but good latency for short responses; open-model path, useful if you want self-hosted reproducibility.
3) Mistral-Instruct-7B (q5) — Very cost-efficient with good quality for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) use cases; great for high-throughput endpoints.
4) Redwood-Base-7B-quant — Lowest cost and fastest latency; good for short, low-complexity answers and hallucination-tolerant tasks.

Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt templates we used), acme_eval_prompts.csv (gold/dev prompts), acme_benchmark_results.pdf (latency/cost/quality charts). Also linking our benchmark page with the raw numbers.

Rationale + tradeoffs (short):
- Quality: Redwood-Instruct-13B-v1 > Llama-2-13B-chat ≈ Mistral-Instruct-7B > Redwood-Base-7B-quant (measured on your eval prompts). If you need the highest factual accuracy for longer answers, start with Redwood-Instruct-13B-v1.
- Latency: Redwood-Base-7B-quant < Mistral-7B (q5) < Redwood-Instruct-13B (optimized q4/q5 path) < Llama-2-13B-chat (q4f16 has slightly higher per-token cost). For sub-200ms token latency on dedicated GPUs we recommend Redwood-Base-7B-quant or Mistral-7B; for 13B models we can hit ~220–300ms depending on batch size and KV caching.
- Cost: Mistral-Instruct-7B and Redwood-Base-7B-quant are cheapest per-token; Redwood-Instruct-13B-v1 is mid-range; Llama-2-13B-chat is highest when using higher-precision quantization.

Security/hosting notes:
- For Private/VPC deployments: we recommend pinned model versions + HSM-backed KMS for keys. Quantized artifacts are stored in customer VPC storage; inference artifacts never leave your network in Private mode.
- Quantization: q4/q5 across 7B/13B works well; we favor q5 for Mistral to keep slightly better FP fidelity at lower cost. For the highest accuracy use q4 for 13B instruct variants.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Your engineering team runs the attached prompt set against the 3 models we recommend (we included Docker-compose artifacts in the eval doc).
2) We can schedule a 1-hour deep-dive with our inference team to tune batching/KV cache for the endpoints you plan to deploy.
3) Rafael can scope a Dedicated capacity estimate if you share expected QPS and SLA.

If you want, Rafael and I can join your Monday sync to present the shortlist.

Thanks — attaching the files now.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo today — quick follow-ups

Jordan — adding the sizing and cost ballpark here. Quick notes before the numbers: we assumed 100k queries/month, avg 120 tokens response, P50 token length 60, P95 220; 50% cache hit rate (prefix/KV) for commonly asked internal questions.

Estimated monthly cost (hosted Dedicated capacity, committed, with burst):
- Redwood-Instruct-13B-v1: ~$8,500/month (includes reserved GPU + inference infra amortized).
- Llama-2-13B-chat (quant q4f16): ~$10,500/month (higher GPU memory overhead increases instance count).
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (q5): ~$4,200/month.
- Redwood-Base-7B-quant: ~$3,100/month.

Latency expectations (tail of request path with conservative tuning):
- Redwood-Base-7B-quant: ~90–140ms per token (short responses <200ms typical)
- Mistral-7B: ~110–160ms per token
- Redwood-Instruct-13B-v1: ~220–300ms per token
- Llama-2-13B-chat: ~240–350ms per token

Top failure modes for Redwood-Instruct-13B-v1 on your evals (high-level):
1) Outdated doc snapshots: occasionally returns references to internal docs that were superseded — remediate by stricter retrieval filters and document versioning in the RAG pipeline.
2) Multi-hop facts: in multi-document syntheses it sometimes hallucinates connector sentences; a few prompt templates reduced this (see attached).
3) Edge-case config names: misses uncommon internal config keys (low frequency) — add targeted prompt examples to the dev set.

Action items: 
- Marissa / Priyom: schedule a tuning call (I can attend).
- Jordan: if you send expected QPS and a sample of your RAG retrieval size we’ll finalize the Dedicated SOW and committed capacity numbers.

Rafael Mendes
Head of Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
